root_cause.text: The function `thermal_of_cm_lookup()` acquires a device node reference via `of_parse_phandle()` but never releases it, causing a reference count leak that can lead to resource exhaustion.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "tr_np is obtained via of_parse_phandle(), but never released." The patch introduces `__free(device_node)` to automatically release the node, confirming the leak was due to a missing `of_node_put()` call.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states "tr_np is obtained via of_parse_phandle(), but never released." The patch introduces `__free(device_node)` to automatically release the node, confirming the leak was due to a missing `of_node_put()` call.

candidates.rationale: This statement acquires a reference to the device node via of_parse_phandle, incrementing its reference count. The function never calls of_node_put to release it, causing a reference leak.

This conditional check uses the acquired device node reference without releasing it. If the condition is true, the subsequent continue statement will skip any code that might release the reference, directly contributing to the leak.

The continue statement causes the loop to skip the remainder of the body, including any potential (but nonexistent) release of the device node reference. It ensures that the reference acquired on line 286 is never released when the trip does not match.

This loop iterates over child nodes and defines the scope within which the device node reference is acquired but not released. While the macro automatically releases the child node, it does not handle the reference obtained from of_parse_phandle, making this the outer structure of the vulnerability.

This declaration creates the variable that holds the acquired device node reference. The reference count management is tied to this variable; without it, the resource acquisition would not be possible, and its lifetime is never properly terminated.

    thermal/of: Fix cdev lookup in thermal_of_should_bind()
    
    Since thermal_of_should_bind() terminates the loop after processing
    the first child found in cooling-maps, it will never match more than
    one cdev to a given trip point which is incorrect, as there may be

bic_trace_step.reason: The new thermal_of_cm_lookup() function acquires a device node reference via of_parse_phandle(child, "trip", 0) but never releases it with of_node_put(). If tr_np != trip->priv, the continue skips the rest of the loop without putting the reference; if a match is found and true is returned, the reference is also not released; if the loop ends without matching, the reference remains held. This causes a reference count leak.
